verses.12:33: Sell your possessions and give alms; make for yourselves money bags that do not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in the heavens, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
verses.12:34: For where your treasure is, there your heart will also be.
verses.12:35: Let your waists be belted and your lamps burning,
verses.12:36: and be like people waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.
verses.12:37: Blessed are those servants whom the master will find staying awake when he comes. Truly I say to you that he will fasten his belt, have them recline at table, and come forward and serve them.
verses.12:38: Whether he comes in the second watch or in the third watch and finds them so, blessed are they.
verses.12:39: Now know this: if the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
verses.12:40: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect."
verses.12:41: Then Peter said, "Lord, are You speaking this parable to us, or also to everyone?"
verses.12:42: And the Lord said, "Who then is the faithful, sensible steward whom the master will put in charge of his household staff, to give them their ration of food at the proper time?
verses.12:43: Blessed is that servant whom his master will find doing so when he comes.
verses.12:44: In truth I say to you that he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
verses.12:45: But if that servant says in his heart, 'My master is delayed in coming,' and begins to beat the male servants and the female servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
verses.12:46: the master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign his portion with the unfaithful.
verses.12:47: And that servant who knew his master's will and did not get ready or act according to his will will be beaten with many blows;
verses.12:48: but the one who did not know, yet did things deserving blows, will be beaten with few. From everyone to whom much was given, much will be required; and from the one to whom much was entrusted, even more will be asked.
verses.12:49: I came to cast fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
verses.12:50: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
verses.12:51: Do you suppose that I came to give peace on earth? No, I say to you, but rather division.
verses.12:52: For from now on five in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three;
verses.12:53: they will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law."
verses.12:54: And He was also saying to the crowds, "When you see a cloud rising in the west, immediately you say, 'A shower is coming,' and so it happens.
verses.12:55: And when a south wind is blowing, you say, 'There will be scorching heat,' and it happens.
verses.12:56: Hypocrites! You know how to discern the appearance of the earth and the sky, yet how is it that you do not know how to discern this present time?
verses.12:57: And why do you not even judge for yourselves what is right?
verses.12:58: For as you are going with your opponent before a magistrate, make an effort on the way to settle with him, so that he does not drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
verses.12:59: I say to you, you will certainly not come out from there until you have paid even the very last coin."
verses.13:1: Now some people were present at that very time, reporting to Him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
verses.13:2: And answering, He said to them, "Do you suppose that these Galileans were greater sinners than all the Galileans because they have suffered these things?
verses.13:3: No, I say to you, but unless you repent, all of you will perish similarly.
verses.13:4: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you suppose that they were greater offenders than all the people dwelling in Jerusalem?
verses.13:5: No, I tell you, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way."
verses.13:6: And He was telling this parable: "A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it and did not find any.
verses.13:7: So he said to the vinedresser, 'Look, for three years I have been coming looking for fruit on this fig tree, and I find none. Cut it down! Why does it even waste the ground?'
verses.13:8: But he answered and said to him, 'Sir, leave it this year also, until I dig around it and put manure on it;
verses.13:9: and if indeed it bears fruit in the time to come—but if not, you will cut it down.'"
verses.13:10: Now He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
verses.13:11: And look, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years, and she was bent over and unable to straighten up at all.
verses.13:12: When Jesus saw her, He called to her and said to her, "Woman, you have been released from your infirmity,"
verses.13:13: and He laid His hands on her; and immediately she was made straight, and she began glorifying God.
verses.13:14: But the synagogue leader, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, responded and was saying to the crowd, "There are six days in which it is necessary to work; so come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day."
verses.13:15: But the Lord answered him and said, "Hypocrites! Does not each of you untie his ox or his donkey from the feeding trough on the Sabbath and lead it away to give it water?
verses.13:16: And this woman, being a daughter of Abraham whom Satan has bound—look, for eighteen years—should she not be released from this bond on the Sabbath day?"
verses.13:17: And as He was saying these things, all those opposing Him were being put to shame, while the entire crowd was rejoicing over all the glorious deeds being done by Him.
verses.13:18: Therefore He was saying, "What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?
verses.13:19: It is like a mustard seed, which a man took and cast into his own garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches."
verses.13:20: And again He said, "To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
verses.13:21: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until all of it was leavened."
verses.13:22: And He was passing through cities and villages, teaching and making His journey toward Jerusalem.
verses.13:23: And someone said to Him, "Lord, are those who are being saved few?" And He said to them,
verses.13:24: "Strive to enter through the narrow door, because many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able,
verses.13:25: once the master of the house gets up and locks the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock on the door, saying, 'Lord, open for us!' Then answering, He will say to you, 'I do not know you—where you are from.'
verses.13:26: Then you will begin to say, 'We ate and drank in Your presence, and You taught in our streets.'
verses.13:27: And He will speak, saying to you, 'I do not know where you are from; depart from Me, all you workers of unrighteousness.'
verses.13:28: In that place there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves being thrown outside.
verses.13:29: And they will come from east and west, and from north and south, and will recline at table in the kingdom of God.
verses.13:30: And look, there are last ones who will be first, and there are first ones who will be last."
verses.13:31: At that very hour some Pharisees came up, saying to Him, "Leave and go away from here, because Herod wants to kill You."
verses.13:32: And He said to them, "Go and tell that fox, 'Look, I am casting out demons and completing healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I reach completion.'
verses.13:33: Nevertheless, I must journey on today and tomorrow and the next day, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.
verses.13:34: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the one who kills the prophets and stones those who have been sent to her—how often I wanted to gather your children together, in the way a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
verses.13:35: Look, your house is left to you. And I tell you, you will certainly not see Me until the time comes when you say, 'Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
verses.14:1: And it happened, when He went into the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, that they were watching Him closely.
verses.14:2: And look, a certain man suffering from dropsy was in front of Him.
verses.14:3: And answering, Jesus spoke to the experts in the law and the Pharisees, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath, or not?"
verses.14:4: But they remained silent. And taking hold of him, He healed him and sent him away.
verses.14:5: And He said to them, "Which of you will have a son or an ox fall into a well, and will not immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?"
verses.14:6: And they were not able to reply to these things.
verses.14:7: Now He began telling a parable to those who had been invited, noticing how they were choosing the places of honor, saying to them,
verses.14:8: "When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast, do not recline in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited by him,
verses.14:9: and the one who invited both you and him will come and say to you, 'Give place to this man,' and then with shame you will begin to take the lowest place.
verses.14:10: Rather, when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, so that when the one who has invited you comes, he will say to you, 'Friend, move up higher.' Then you will have honor in the presence of all who recline at table with you.
verses.14:11: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted."
verses.14:12: And He was also saying to the one who had invited Him, "When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not invite your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors, in case they also invite you in return and repayment comes to you.
verses.14:13: Instead, when you give a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind;
verses.14:14: and you will be blessed, because they cannot repay you; for you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."
verses.14:15: When one of those reclining at table heard these things, he said to Him, "Blessed is whoever will eat bread in the kingdom of God!"
verses.14:16: But He said to him, "A certain man was giving a great banquet, and he invited many;
verses.14:17: and at the hour of the banquet he sent his slave to say to those who had been invited, 'Come, because everything is ready now.'
verses.14:18: And they all alike began to make excuses. The first said to him, 'I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it; I ask you, consider me excused.'
verses.14:19: And another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am on my way to try them out; I ask you, consider me excused.'
verses.14:20: And another said, 'I have married a wife, and for that reason I cannot come.'
verses.14:21: And the slave came back and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house became angry and said to his slave, 'Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in here the poor and crippled and blind and lame.'
verses.14:22: And the slave said, 'Master, what you commanded has been done, and still there is room.'
verses.14:23: And the master said to the slave, 'Go out to the roads and hedges and compel people to come in, so that my house may be filled;
verses.14:24: for I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my banquet.'"
verses.14:25: Now large crowds were traveling along with Him, and turning around, He said to them,
verses.14:26: "If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own life, he cannot be My disciple.
verses.14:27: Whoever does not carry his cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple.
verses.14:28: For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the cost, to see whether he has enough for its completion?
verses.14:29: Otherwise, after he has laid a foundation and is unable to finish, all who look on may begin to mock him,
verses.14:30: saying, 'This man began to build and was not able to finish.'
verses.14:31: Or what king, going out to engage another king in war, will not first sit down and take counsel whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
verses.14:32: And if not, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace.
verses.14:33: In the same way, therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all his own possessions cannot be My disciple.
verses.14:34: Salt, therefore, is good; but if even salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be seasoned?
verses.14:35: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile; they throw it out. The one who has ears to hear, let him hear."
verses.15:1: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners were drawing near to Him to listen to Him.
verses.15:2: And both the Pharisees and the scribes were grumbling, saying, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them."
verses.15:3: So He spoke this parable to them, saying,
verses.15:4: "What man among you, having a hundred sheep and having lost one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine behind in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?
verses.15:5: And when he has found it, he lays it upon his shoulders, rejoicing.
verses.15:6: And when he comes into the house, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost.'
verses.15:7: I tell you that in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.
verses.15:8: Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?
verses.15:9: And when she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma that I lost.'
verses.15:10: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
verses.15:11: And He said, "A certain man had two sons.
verses.15:12: And the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the share of the estate that falls to me.' So he divided his livelihood between them.
verses.15:13: And not many days later, having gathered everything together, the younger son journeyed away to a distant country, and there he squandered his estate by living recklessly.
verses.15:14: Now when he had spent everything, a severe famine occurred throughout that country, and he himself began to be in need.
verses.15:15: So he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
verses.15:16: And he was longing to be filled from the carob pods that the pigs were eating, and no one was giving anything to him.
verses.15:17: But when he came to himself, he said, 'How many of my father's hired workers have an abundance of bread, while I am perishing here from hunger!
verses.15:18: I will get up and go to my father and say to him, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight;
verses.15:19: I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me like one of your hired workers."'
verses.15:20: And he got up and came to his own father. But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and he ran and fell upon his neck and kissed him affectionately.
verses.15:21: And the son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.'
verses.15:22: But the father said to his slaves, 'Quickly bring out the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet,
verses.15:23: and bring the fattened calf, slaughter it, and let us eat and celebrate,
verses.15:24: because this son of mine was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found.' And they began to celebrate.
verses.15:25: Now his older son was in the field; and as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
verses.15:26: And calling over one of the servants, he began inquiring what these things might be.
verses.15:27: And he said to him, 'Your brother has arrived, and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and sound.'
verses.15:28: But he became angry and was unwilling to go in. So his father came out and was pleading with him.
verses.15:29: But he answered and said to his father, 'Look, for so many years I have been serving you and have never neglected a command of yours, yet to me you have never given a young goat so that I might celebrate with my friends;
verses.15:30: but when this son of yours came, who has devoured your livelihood with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him.'
verses.15:31: And he said to him, 'Child, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
verses.15:32: Yet it was necessary to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come to life, and was lost and has been found.'"
verses.16:1: Now He was also saying to the disciples, "There was a certain rich man who had a manager, and this man was accused to him of squandering his possessions.
verses.16:2: And calling him, he said to him, 'What is this I hear about you? Turn in the account of your management, for you can no longer be manager.'
verses.16:3: Then the manager said to himself, 'What will I do, since my master is taking the management away from me? I am not strong enough to dig; I am ashamed to beg.
verses.16:4: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from the management, they will welcome me into their own homes.'
verses.16:5: And summoning each one of his master's debtors, he said to the first, 'How much do you owe my master?'
verses.16:6: And he said, 'A hundred baths of olive oil.' And he said to him, 'Take your bill, sit down quickly, and write fifty.'
verses.16:7: Then he said to another, 'And how much do you owe?' And he said, 'A hundred kors of wheat.' He says to him, 'Take your bill and write eighty.'
verses.16:8: And the master commended the unrighteous manager because he had acted shrewdly; for the sons of this age are more shrewd than the sons of light toward their own generation.
verses.16:9: And I tell you, make friends for yourselves from unrighteous wealth, so that when it fails, they may welcome you into the eternal dwellings.
verses.16:10: One who is faithful in very little is also faithful in much, and one who is unrighteous in very little is also unrighteous in much.
verses.16:11: Therefore, if you have not been faithful with unrighteous wealth, who will entrust to you what is true?
verses.16:12: And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?
verses.16:13: No household servant can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold fast to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth."
verses.16:14: Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, were listening to all these things and were scoffing at Him.
verses.16:15: And He said to them, "You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of people, but God knows your hearts; for what is exalted among people is an abomination in the sight of God.
verses.16:16: The Law and the Prophets were until John; since that time the good news of the kingdom of God is being proclaimed, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
verses.16:17: Yet it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a letter of the Law to fall.
verses.16:18: Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and the one who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.
verses.16:19: Now there was a certain rich man, and he habitually dressed in purple and fine linen, feasting splendidly every day.
verses.16:20: And a certain poor man named Lazarus had been laid at his gate, covered with sores,
verses.16:21: and longing to be filled from what fell from the rich man's table; moreover, even the dogs would come and lick his sores.
verses.16:22: Now it happened that the poor man died and was carried away by the angels to Abraham's side; and the rich man also died and was buried.
verses.16:23: And in Hades, lifting up his eyes, being in torment, he sees Abraham from a distance and Lazarus at his side.
verses.16:24: And he called out and said, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus so that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am in agony in this flame.'
verses.16:25: But Abraham said, 'Child, remember that you received your good things during your lifetime, and Lazarus likewise bad things; yet now he is being comforted here, while you are in agony.
verses.16:26: And besides all these things, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, so that those who wish to cross over from here to you are not able, nor may any cross over from there to us.'
verses.16:27: And he said, 'Then I beg you, father, to send him to my father's house,
verses.16:28: for I have five brothers, so that he may solemnly warn them, so that they will not also come into this place of torment.'
verses.16:29: But Abraham says, 'They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to them.'
verses.16:30: And he said, 'No, father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.'
verses.16:31: But he said to him, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.'"
verses.17:1: Now He said to His disciples, "It is impossible for stumbling blocks not to come, yet woe to the one through whom they come!
verses.17:2: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck and he were cast into the sea than for him to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
verses.17:3: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.
verses.17:4: And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times turns back to you saying, 'I repent,' you shall forgive him."
verses.17:5: And the apostles said to the Lord, "Increase our faith."
verses.17:6: And the Lord said, "If you have faith like a mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
verses.17:7: Now which of you, having a slave plowing or tending sheep, will say to him when he comes in from the field, 'Come forward at once and recline at table,'
verses.17:8: and will not instead say to him, 'Prepare something for me to eat for supper, and fasten your belt and serve me while I eat and drink, and after that you yourself will eat and drink'?
verses.17:9: He does not thank the slave because he did the things that were commanded, does he?
verses.17:10: So you also, when you have done all the things commanded you, say, 'We are unworthy slaves; we have done what we were obligated to do.'"
verses.17:11: And it happened while He was traveling to Jerusalem that He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
verses.17:12: And as He was entering a certain village, ten leprous men met Him, who stood at a distance,
verses.17:13: and they lifted up their voices, saying, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"
verses.17:14: And when He saw them, He said to them, "Go and show yourselves to the priests." And it happened that as they were going, they were cleansed.
verses.17:15: Now one of them, when he saw that he had been healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice,
verses.17:16: and he fell on his face at His feet, giving thanks to Him. And he was a Samaritan.
verses.17:17: Then Jesus answered and said, "Were not the ten cleansed? Yet where are the nine?
verses.17:18: Were none found who turned back to give glory to God except this foreigner?"
verses.17:19: And He said to him, "Get up and go; your faith has saved you."
verses.17:20: Now having been questioned by the Pharisees as to when the kingdom of God is coming, He answered them and said, "The kingdom of God does not come with observation,
verses.17:21: nor will they say, 'Look, here!' or, 'There!' For look, the kingdom of God is in your midst."
verses.17:22: And He said to the disciples, "Days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
verses.17:23: And they will say to you, 'Look, there!' or, 'Look, here!' Do not go off, nor pursue them.
verses.17:24: For just as the lightning, flashing from one side under heaven, shines to the other under heaven, so will the Son of Man be in His day.
verses.17:25: But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
verses.17:26: And just as it happened in the days of Noah, so it will also be in the days of the Son of Man:
verses.17:27: they were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came and destroyed all of them.
verses.17:28: Likewise, just as it happened in the days of Lot: they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building;
verses.17:29: but on the day Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from heaven and destroyed all of them.
verses.17:30: In the very same way it will be on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
verses.17:31: On that day, let the one who is on the housetop, with his belongings in the house, not come down to take them away; and likewise let the one in the field not turn back to what is behind.
verses.17:33: Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will keep it alive.
verses.17:34: I tell you, on that night there will be two in one bed; one will be taken and the other will be left.
verses.17:35: There will be two women grinding together; one will be taken, and the other will be left."
verses.17:37: And answering, they said to Him, "Where, Lord?" And He said to them, "Where the body is, there the vultures will also be gathered together."
verses.18:1: Now He was telling a parable to them about how they must always pray and not lose heart,
verses.18:2: saying, "There was a certain judge in a certain city who did not fear God and did not respect man.
verses.18:3: And there was a widow in that city, and she kept coming to him, saying, 'Give me justice against my adversary.'
verses.18:4: And for a time he was unwilling, but afterward he said within himself, 'Even though I do not fear God nor respect man,
verses.18:5: yet because this widow causes me trouble, I will give her justice, so that by continually coming she will not wear me out.'"
verses.18:6: And the Lord said, "Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.
verses.18:7: And will God not certainly bring about justice for His chosen ones who cry out to Him day and night, while He is patient over them?
verses.18:8: I tell you that He will bring about justice for them quickly. However, when the Son of Man comes, will He indeed find the faith on the earth?"
verses.18:9: He also told this parable to some who were confident in themselves that they were righteous and treated the rest with contempt:
verses.18:10: "Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
verses.18:11: The Pharisee, taking his stand, prayed these things to himself: 'God, I thank You that I am not like the rest of people—extortioners, unjust, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
verses.18:12: I fast twice a week; I tithe everything that I acquire.'
verses.18:13: But the tax collector, standing at a distance, was unwilling even to lift up his eyes toward heaven, but kept beating his chest, saying, 'God, be merciful to me, the sinner!'
verses.18:14: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than that one; because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted."
verses.18:15: Now they were bringing even infants to Him so that He might touch them; but when the disciples saw it, they were rebuking them.
verses.18:16: But Jesus called them to Himself, saying, "Allow the little children to come to Me and do not hinder them, for to such as these belongs the kingdom of God.
verses.18:17: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will by no means enter into it."
verses.18:18: And a certain ruler questioned Him, saying, "Good Teacher, by doing what will I inherit eternal life?"
verses.18:19: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One—God.
verses.18:20: You know the commandments: 'Do not commit adultery,' 'Do not murder,' 'Do not steal,' 'Do not bear false witness,' 'Honor your father and mother.'"
verses.18:21: And he said, "All these things I have kept from my youth."
verses.18:22: When Jesus heard this, He said to him, "Still one thing you lack: sell everything that you possess and distribute it to the poor, and you will have treasure in the heavens; and come, follow Me."
verses.18:23: But when he heard these things, he became deeply grieved, for he was exceedingly wealthy.
verses.18:24: And seeing him, Jesus said, "With what difficulty those who have wealth enter into the kingdom of God!
verses.18:25: For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God."
verses.18:26: And those who heard it said, "Then who is able to be saved?"
verses.18:27: But He said, "Things impossible with men are possible with God."
verses.18:28: And Peter said, "Look, we have left everything and followed You."
verses.18:29: And He said to them, "Truly I tell you that there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,
verses.18:30: who will not certainly receive many times as much in this time, and in the coming age eternal life."
verses.18:31: Taking the twelve aside, He said to them, "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything written through the prophets for the Son of Man will be accomplished.
verses.18:32: For He will be handed over to the Gentiles, and will be mocked and shamefully treated and spit upon;
verses.18:33: and after flogging Him, they will kill Him, and on the third day He will rise."
verses.18:34: And they themselves understood none of these things, and this saying was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend the things being spoken.
verses.18:35: Now it happened that as He was drawing near to Jericho, a certain blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
verses.18:36: And hearing a crowd passing by, he began inquiring what this might be.
verses.18:37: And they reported to him that Jesus the Nazarene was passing by.
verses.18:38: And he cried out, saying, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
verses.18:39: And those going ahead were rebuking him so that he would be silent, but he kept shouting all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
verses.18:40: And Jesus stopped and ordered him to be brought to Him. And when he drew near, He asked him,
verses.18:41: "What do you want Me to do for you?" And he said, "Lord, that I may regain my sight."
verses.18:42: And Jesus said to him, "Regain your sight; your faith has saved you."
verses.18:43: And immediately he regained his sight and began following Him, glorifying God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.
verses.19:1: And having entered, He was passing through Jericho.
verses.19:2: And look, there was a man called by name Zacchaeus; and he was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
verses.19:3: And he was seeking to see who Jesus was, and he was unable because of the crowd, for he was small in stature.
verses.19:4: So running on ahead, he climbed up into a sycamore-fig tree in order to see Him, because He was about to pass by that way.
verses.19:5: And when He came to the place, Jesus looked up and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house."
verses.19:6: And he hurried and came down, and welcomed Him rejoicing.
verses.19:7: And when they saw it, they all kept grumbling, saying, "He has gone in to lodge with a sinful man."
verses.19:8: But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, "Look, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I pay back fourfold."
verses.19:9: And Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham;
verses.19:10: for the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost."
verses.19:11: Now as they were listening to these things, He went on to tell a parable, because He was near Jerusalem and they supposed that the kingdom of God was about to appear immediately.
verses.19:12: So He said, "A certain man of noble birth journeyed to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and to return.
verses.19:13: And calling ten of his slaves, he gave them ten minas and said to them, 'Conduct business until I come.'
verses.19:14: But his citizens hated him, and they sent a delegation after him, saying, 'We do not want this man to reign over us.'
verses.19:15: And it happened when he returned, having received the kingdom, that he ordered these slaves to whom he had given the money to be summoned to him, so that he might know what they had gained by doing business.
verses.19:16: Then the first came forward, saying, 'Master, your mina has earned ten more minas.'
verses.19:17: And he said to him, 'Well done, good slave! Because you proved faithful in a very small matter, have authority over ten cities.'
verses.19:18: And the second came, saying, 'Your mina, master, has made five minas.'
verses.19:19: And he said to this one also, 'You also be over five cities.'
verses.19:20: And the other came, saying, 'Master, here is your mina, which I kept put away in a handkerchief;
verses.19:21: for I was afraid of you, because you are a severe man: you take up what you did not lay down, and you reap what you did not sow.'
verses.19:22: He says to him, 'Out of your mouth I judge you, wicked slave! You knew that I am a severe man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow?
verses.19:23: Then why did you not put my money in the bank? And upon coming, I would have collected it with interest.'
verses.19:24: And he said to those standing by, 'Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has the ten minas'—
verses.19:25: and they said to him, 'Master, he has ten minas'—
verses.19:26: 'I say to you that to everyone who has, it will be given, but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
verses.19:27: But as for these enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slaughter them before me.'"
verses.19:28: And having said these things, He was going on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
verses.19:29: And it happened as He drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called Olivet, that He sent two of the disciples,
verses.19:30: saying, "Go into the village opposite, where on entering you will find a colt tied, on which no person has ever yet sat; untie it and bring it.
verses.19:31: And if anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?' you will say this: 'The Lord has need of it.'"
verses.19:32: So those who had been sent departed and found it just as He had told them.
verses.19:33: And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, "Why are you untying the colt?"
verses.19:34: And they said, "The Lord has need of it."
verses.19:35: And they brought it to Jesus, and throwing their cloaks onto the colt, they set Jesus on it.
verses.19:36: And as He went along, they were spreading their cloaks on the road.
verses.19:37: And as He was already drawing near to the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began, rejoicing, to praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen,
verses.19:38: saying, "Blessed is the King coming in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!"
verses.19:39: And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to Him, "Teacher, rebuke Your disciples."
verses.19:40: And in reply He said, "I tell you that if these stay silent, the stones will cry out."
verses.19:41: And as He drew near, seeing the city, He wept over it,
verses.19:42: saying, "If only you too had known on this day the things that lead to peace—but now they have been hidden from your eyes.
verses.19:43: For days will come upon you when your enemies will set up a barricade around you, and encircle you, and hem you in on every side,
verses.19:44: and they will dash you to the ground, and your children within you, and they will not leave one stone upon another in you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation."
verses.19:45: And having entered the temple, He began to drive out those who were selling,
verses.19:46: saying to them, "It is written, 'My house is a house of prayer,' but you have made it a cave of robbers."
verses.19:47: And He was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes were seeking to destroy Him, and the leading men of the people also,
verses.19:48: and they could not find what they might do, for all the people were hanging on Him as they listened.
verses.20:1: And it happened on one of the days, while He was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the good news, that the chief priests and the scribes, together with the elders, came up,
verses.20:2: and they spoke, saying to Him, "Tell us by what authority You are doing these things, or who is the one who gave You this authority?"
verses.20:3: And answering, He said to them, "I will also ask you a question, and tell Me:
verses.20:4: The baptism of John, was it from heaven or from men?"
verses.20:5: And they reasoned together among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say, 'Why did you not believe him?'
verses.20:6: But if we say, 'From men,' all the people will stone us to death, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."
verses.20:7: And they answered that they did not know where it was from.
verses.20:8: And Jesus said to them, "Neither am I telling you by what authority I am doing these things."
verses.20:9: And He began to tell the people this parable: "A man planted a vineyard, and leased it to farmers, and went abroad for a considerable time.
verses.20:10: And at the proper time he sent a slave to the farmers, so that they would give him some of the fruit of the vineyard; but the farmers beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
verses.20:11: And he proceeded to send another slave; but they beat and dishonored that one also, and sent him away empty-handed.
verses.20:12: And he proceeded to send a third; and they wounded this one also and threw him out.
verses.20:13: Then the owner of the vineyard said, 'What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.'
verses.20:14: But when the farmers saw him, they reasoned with one another, saying, 'This is the heir; let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours.'
verses.20:15: And throwing him out of the vineyard, they killed him. What therefore will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
verses.20:16: He will come and destroy these farmers, and will give the vineyard to others." And when they heard this, they said, "May it never be!"
verses.20:17: But looking intently at them, He said, "What then is this that is written: 'The stone that the builders rejected, this became the chief cornerstone'?
verses.20:18: Everyone who falls on that stone will be broken to pieces; but on whomever it falls, it will crush him to powder."
verses.20:19: And the scribes and the chief priests sought to lay hands on Him in that very hour, yet they feared the people, for they knew that He spoke this parable against them.
verses.20:20: And watching closely, they sent spies who pretended to be righteous, so that they might catch Him in a statement, so as to hand Him over to the rule and the authority of the governor.
verses.20:21: And they questioned Him, saying, "Teacher, we know that You speak and teach rightly, and do not show partiality, but truly teach the way of God:
verses.20:22: Is it lawful for us to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?"
verses.20:23: But perceiving their craftiness, He said to them,
verses.20:24: "Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have?" And they said, "Caesar's."
verses.20:25: And He said to them, "Then give back to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's."
verses.20:26: And they were not able to take hold of what He said before the people; and marveling at His answer, they became silent.
verses.20:27: Now some of the Sadducees, those who say that there is no resurrection, came up and questioned Him,
verses.20:28: saying, "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
verses.20:29: Now there were seven brothers; and the first took a wife and died childless;
verses.20:31: and the third took her; and in the same way the seven also left no children and died.
verses.20:33: In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife among them does she become? For the seven had her as a wife."
verses.20:34: And Jesus said to them, "The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage,
verses.20:35: but those who are considered worthy to attain to that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage;
verses.20:36: for they cannot even die anymore, because they are equal to angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
verses.20:37: But that the dead are raised, even Moses made known in the passage about the bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
verses.20:38: Now He is not the God of the dead, but of the living; for all live to Him."
verses.20:39: And some of the scribes answered and said, "Teacher, You have spoken well."
verses.20:40: For they no longer dared to ask Him anything.
verses.20:41: And He said to them, "How do they say that the Christ is David's son?
verses.20:42: For David himself says in the book of Psalms, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand,
verses.20:43: until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet."'
verses.20:44: David therefore calls Him Lord, and how is He his son?"
verses.20:45: And while all the people were listening, He said to His disciples,
verses.20:46: "Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk around in long robes, and love greetings in the marketplaces, and the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets,
verses.20:47: who devour widows' houses, and for a pretense make long prayers. These will receive greater condemnation."
verses.21:1: And looking up, He saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.
verses.21:2: And He saw a certain needy widow putting two lepta there,
verses.21:3: and He said, "Truly I tell you that this poor widow put in more than all of them;
verses.21:4: for all of these put into the gifts out of their surplus, but she out of her lack put in all the livelihood that she had."
verses.21:5: And as some were speaking about the temple, that it was adorned with fine stones and dedicated offerings, He said,
verses.21:6: "As for these things that you are observing, days will come in which a stone will not be left upon a stone that will not be torn down."
verses.21:7: And they questioned Him, saying, "Teacher, when therefore will these things be, and what is the sign when these things are about to take place?"
verses.21:8: And He said, "Watch out that you are not misled; for many will come in My name, saying, 'I am,' and, 'The time has drawn near.' Do not go after them.
verses.21:9: And when you hear of wars and disturbances, do not be terrified; for these things must take place first, but the end is not immediately."
verses.21:10: Then He was saying to them, "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom,
verses.21:11: and there will be great earthquakes, and in various places famines and plagues, and there will be terrors and great signs from heaven.
verses.21:12: But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to the synagogues and prisons, as you are brought before kings and governors on account of My name.
verses.21:13: It will turn out for you as a testimony.
verses.21:14: Settle it therefore in your hearts not to prepare beforehand to make a defense,
verses.21:15: for I will give you a mouth and wisdom that all those opposing you will not be able to resist or contradict.
verses.21:16: Yet you will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death,
verses.21:17: and you will be hated by all because of My name.
verses.21:18: And not a hair from your head will by any means perish.
verses.21:19: By your endurance, gain your souls.
verses.21:20: And when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has drawn near.
verses.21:21: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those who are in the midst of it depart, and let those who are in the countryside not enter into it,
verses.21:22: because these are days of vengeance, so that all things that have been written may be fulfilled.
verses.21:23: Woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days; for there will be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people,
verses.21:24: and they will fall by the edge of the sword and will be taken captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
verses.21:25: And there will be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and on the earth anguish of nations in perplexity at the roaring of the sea and its surging,
verses.21:26: with people fainting from fear and expectation of the things coming upon the inhabited world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
verses.21:27: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
verses.21:28: Now when these things begin to take place, straighten up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near."
verses.21:29: And He spoke a parable to them: "Look at the fig tree and all the trees;
verses.21:30: when they already sprout, seeing it you know for yourselves that summer is already near.
verses.21:31: So also you, when you see these things taking place, know that the kingdom of God is near.
verses.21:32: Truly I tell you that this generation will by no means pass away until all things take place.
verses.21:33: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will by no means pass away.
verses.21:34: But watch yourselves, so that your hearts may not be weighed down with carousing and drunkenness and the anxieties of life, and that day come upon you suddenly
verses.21:35: like a trap; for it will come upon all those who dwell on the face of all the earth.
verses.21:36: But stay awake at all times, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are about to take place, and to stand before the Son of Man."
verses.21:37: Now during the days He was teaching in the temple, but at night He would go out and spend the night on the mount called Olivet;
verses.21:38: and all the people would come early in the morning to Him in the temple to listen to Him.
verses.22:1: Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called the Passover, was drawing near.
verses.22:2: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might do away with Him, for they feared the people.
verses.22:3: Now Satan entered into Judas, the one called Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.
verses.22:4: And he went away and conferred with the chief priests and captains on how he might betray Him to them.
verses.22:5: And they rejoiced and agreed to give him silver.
verses.22:6: And he consented, and was seeking an opportunity to betray Him to them apart from a crowd.
verses.22:7: Now the day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover had to be sacrificed.
verses.22:8: And He sent Peter and John, saying, "Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat."
verses.22:9: Then they said to Him, "Where do You want us to prepare it?"
verses.22:10: And He said to them, "Look, when you have entered the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house that he enters.
verses.22:11: And you will say to the master of the house, 'The Teacher says to you, "Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?"'
verses.22:12: And he will show you a large upper room that has been furnished; prepare it there."
verses.22:13: So they departed and found it just as He had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.22:14: And when the hour arrived, He reclined at table, and the apostles with Him.
verses.22:15: And He said to them, "With longing I have longed to eat this Passover with you before I suffer;
verses.22:16: for I say to you that I will certainly not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
verses.22:17: And having received a cup and given thanks, He said, "Take this and divide it among yourselves;
verses.22:18: for I say to you, from now on I will certainly not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
verses.22:19: And having taken bread and given thanks, He broke it and gave it to them, saying, "This is My body, which is being given for you; do this in remembrance of Me."
verses.22:20: And likewise the cup after they had dined, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is being poured out for you.
verses.22:21: Yet look, the hand of the one betraying Me is with Me on the table.
verses.22:22: For the Son of Man indeed goes according to what has been determined, yet woe to that man through whom He is betrayed."
verses.22:23: And they began to discuss among themselves which of them it might be who was about to do this.
verses.22:24: Now a dispute also arose among them as to which of them was considered to be the greatest.
verses.22:25: And He said to them, "The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and those who hold authority over them are called Benefactors.
verses.22:26: But not so with you; rather, let the greatest among you become like the youngest, and the one who leads like the one who serves.
verses.22:27: For who is greater, the one who reclines at table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines at table? Yet I am in your midst as the one who serves.
verses.22:28: Now you are the ones who have remained with Me in My trials;
verses.22:29: and I confer on you, just as My Father conferred a kingdom on Me,
verses.22:30: so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
verses.22:31: Simon, Simon, look, Satan has demanded to have you, to sift you like wheat;
verses.22:32: but I have pleaded for you that your faith may not fail; and you, once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers."
verses.22:33: And he said to Him, "Lord, with You I am prepared to go both into prison and to death."
verses.22:34: And He said, "I tell you, Peter, a rooster will not crow today until you have three times denied knowing Me."
verses.22:35: And He said to them, "When I sent you out without a moneybag or knapsack or sandals, did you lack anything?" And they said, "Nothing."
verses.22:36: Then He said to them, "But now, let the one who has a moneybag take it, and likewise a knapsack; and let the one who has none sell his cloak and buy a sword.
verses.22:37: For I say to you that this which is written must be fulfilled in Me: 'And He was counted with the lawless.' For indeed what concerns Me has its fulfillment."
verses.22:38: And they said, "Lord, see, here are two swords." And He said to them, "That is enough."
verses.22:39: And going out, He proceeded according to custom to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples also followed Him.
verses.22:40: And having arrived at the place, He said to them, "Pray not to enter into temptation."
verses.22:41: And He Himself withdrew from them about a stone's throw, and kneeling down, He was praying,
verses.22:42: saying, "Father, if You are willing, take this cup away from Me; yet let not My will, but Yours, be done."
verses.22:43: Then an angel from heaven appeared to Him, strengthening Him.
verses.22:44: And coming into agony, He was praying more fervently, and His sweat became like thick drops of blood falling onto the ground.
verses.22:45: And rising from prayer, He came to the disciples and found them sleeping from sorrow,
verses.22:46: and He said to them, "Why are you sleeping? Rise up and pray, so that you will not enter into temptation."
verses.22:47: While He was still speaking, look, there was a crowd, and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was going ahead of them; and he drew near to Jesus to kiss Him.
verses.22:48: Then Jesus said to him, "Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?"
verses.22:49: And when those around Him saw what was about to happen, they said, "Lord, should we strike with a sword?"
verses.22:50: And a certain one of them struck the slave of the high priest and cut off his right ear.
verses.22:51: But Jesus answered and said, "Leave it at this!" And touching the ear, He healed him.
verses.22:52: Then Jesus said to the chief priests and captains of the temple and elders who had come against Him, "Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
verses.22:53: While I was with you day by day in the temple, you did not stretch out your hands against Me. But this is your hour, and the authority of darkness."
verses.22:54: Now having seized Him, they led Him away and brought Him into the house of the high priest; and Peter was following at a distance.
verses.22:55: And when they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter was sitting among them.
verses.22:56: And a certain servant girl, seeing him sitting by the light and gazing intently at him, said, "This man also was with Him."
verses.22:57: But he denied it, saying, "I do not know Him, woman."
verses.22:58: And after a little while, another man saw him and said, "You also are one of them." But Peter said, "Man, I am not."
verses.22:59: And after an interval of about an hour, another man kept insisting, saying, "In truth, this man also was with Him, for he indeed is a Galilean."
verses.22:60: But Peter said, "Man, I do not know what you are saying." And immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
verses.22:61: And turning, the Lord looked straight at Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how He had said to him, "Before a rooster crows today, you will deny Me three times."
verses.22:62: And going outside, he wept bitterly.
verses.22:63: Now the men who were holding Him were mocking Him and beating Him,
verses.22:64: and having blindfolded Him, they kept questioning Him, saying, "Prophesy! Who is the one who struck You?"
verses.22:65: And blaspheming, they were saying many other things against Him.
verses.22:66: And when day came, the assembly of elders of the people was gathered together, both chief priests and scribes, and they led Him away into their Sanhedrin,
verses.22:67: saying, "If You are the Christ, tell us." But He said to them, "If I tell you, you will certainly not believe;
verses.22:68: and if I ask a question, you will certainly not answer.
verses.22:69: Yet from now on, the Son of Man will be sitting at the right hand of the power of God."
verses.22:70: Then they all said, "Are You then the Son of God?" And He said to them, "You yourselves say that I am."
verses.22:71: And they said, "Why do we still have need of testimony? For we ourselves have heard it from His mouth."
verses.23:1: And the entire multitude of them rose up and brought Him before Pilate.
verses.23:2: And they began to accuse Him, saying, "We found this man subverting our nation and forbidding the paying of taxes to Caesar, and saying that He Himself is Christ, a king."
verses.23:3: Now Pilate questioned Him, saying, "Are You the King of the Jews?" And He answered him and said, "You say so."
verses.23:4: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, "I find no basis for a charge in this man."
verses.23:5: But they grew more insistent, saying, "He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, beginning even from Galilee as far as here."
verses.23:6: When Pilate heard this, he asked whether the man was a Galilean,
verses.23:7: and when he learned that He was under Herod's jurisdiction, he sent Him up to Herod, who himself was also in Jerusalem in those days.
verses.23:8: Now when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceedingly glad, for he had been desiring for a long time to see Him because of hearing about Him, and he was hoping to see some sign done by Him.
verses.23:9: And he kept questioning Him with many words, yet He answered him nothing.
verses.23:10: And the chief priests and the scribes were standing there, vehemently accusing Him.
verses.23:11: And Herod as well, along with his soldiers, treated Him with contempt and mocked Him, and having dressed Him in a splendid garment, he sent Him back to Pilate.
verses.23:12: And both Herod and Pilate became friends with one another on that very day, for previously they had been at enmity with each other.
verses.23:13: Then Pilate, having called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,
verses.23:14: said to them, "You brought this man to me as one leading the people astray, and look, having examined Him before you, I found no basis for a charge in this man regarding the things of which you accuse Him.
verses.23:15: Nor did Herod either, for he sent Him back to us; and look, nothing deserving of death has been done by Him.
verses.23:16: Therefore I will punish Him and release Him."
verses.23:18: But they all cried out together, saying, "Away with this man, and release Barabbas to us!"
verses.23:19: He was one who had been thrown into prison because of a certain insurrection that had occurred in the city, and for murder.
verses.23:20: Again Pilate addressed them, wanting to release Jesus.
verses.23:21: But they kept shouting out, saying, "Crucify, crucify Him!"
verses.23:22: And a third time he said to them, "Why, what evil has this man done? I found no basis for death in Him. Therefore I will punish Him and release Him."
verses.23:23: But they kept pressing with loud voices, demanding that He be crucified, and their voices prevailed.
verses.23:24: And Pilate ruled that their demand be granted.
verses.23:25: And he released the one who had been thrown into prison for insurrection and murder, whom they were demanding, while Jesus he handed over to their will.
verses.23:26: And as they led Him away, taking hold of a certain Simon, a Cyrenian, coming from the countryside, they laid the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
verses.23:27: And a large multitude of the people was following Him, and of women who were mourning and lamenting for Him.
verses.23:28: But turning to them, Jesus said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me; rather, weep for yourselves and for your children,
verses.23:29: for look, days are coming in which they will say, 'Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not give birth, and the breasts that did not nurse.'
verses.23:30: Then they will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall on us,' and to the hills, 'Cover us,'
verses.23:31: for if they do these things with the green wood, what will happen with the dry?"
verses.23:32: And two others also, who were criminals, were being led out with Him to be put to death.
verses.23:33: And when they arrived at the place called Skull, there they crucified Him and the criminals, one on the right and one on the left.
verses.23:34: And Jesus was saying, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." And dividing His garments among themselves, they cast lots.
verses.23:35: And the people stood watching. And the rulers also were sneering, saying, "He saved others; let Him save Himself if this is the Christ of God, the Chosen One."
verses.23:36: And the soldiers also mocked Him, approaching and offering Him sour wine,
verses.23:37: and saying, "If You are the King of the Jews, save Yourself!"
verses.23:38: Now there was also an inscription over Him: "This is the King of the Jews."
verses.23:39: And one of the criminals who had been hanged was reviling Him, saying, "Are You not the Christ? Save Yourself and us!"
verses.23:40: But answering, the other rebuked him and said, "Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same condemnation?
verses.23:41: And we indeed justly, for we are receiving what we deserve for what we did; but this man has done nothing wrong."
verses.23:42: And he was saying, "Jesus, remember me when You come in Your kingdom."
verses.23:43: And He said to him, "Truly I say to you, today you will be with Me in Paradise."
verses.23:44: Now it was already about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour,
verses.23:45: as the sun failed, and the curtain of the sanctuary was torn down the middle.
verses.23:46: And crying out with a loud voice, Jesus said, "Father, into Your hands I entrust My spirit." And having said this, He breathed His last.
verses.23:47: Now when the centurion saw what had happened, he was glorifying God, saying, "Certainly, this man was righteous."
verses.23:48: And all the crowds who had gathered together for this spectacle, having observed the things that happened, were turning back, beating their breasts.
verses.23:49: And all His acquaintances stood at a distance, as well as the women who had followed with Him from Galilee, watching these things.
verses.23:50: And now there was a man named Joseph, who was a council member, a good and righteous man—
verses.23:51: this man had not consented to their plan and action—from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, who was waiting for the kingdom of God;
verses.23:52: this man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus,
verses.23:53: and having taken it down, he wrapped it in a linen cloth and laid Him in a rock-hewn tomb where no one had yet been laid.
verses.23:54: And it was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was dawning.
verses.23:55: Now the women who had come with Him from Galilee followed closely behind, and they observed the tomb and how His body was laid.
verses.23:56: Then returning, they prepared spices and perfumes. And on the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.
verses.24:1: Now on the first day of the week, at very early dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices that they had prepared.
verses.24:2: And they found that the stone had been rolled away from the tomb,
verses.24:3: and when they went in, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
verses.24:4: And it happened, while they were perplexed about this, look, two men stood beside them in dazzling clothing.
verses.24:5: And as they became terrified and bowed their faces to the ground, they said to them, "Why are you seeking the Living One among the dead?
verses.24:6: He is not here, but has been raised. Remember how He spoke to you while He was still in Galilee,
verses.24:7: saying that the Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise."
verses.24:9: and having returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
verses.24:10: Now they were Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them; they were telling these things to the apostles.
verses.24:11: And these words appeared before them like nonsense, and they disbelieved them.
verses.24:12: But Peter rose and ran to the tomb; and stooping down to look in, he saw the linen cloths alone; and he went away to his home, marveling at what had happened.
verses.24:13: And look, two of them on that very day were traveling to a village sixty stadia distant from Jerusalem, whose name was Emmaus,
verses.24:14: and they were conversing with one another about all these things that had taken place.
verses.24:15: And it happened, while they were conversing and discussing, that Jesus Himself drew near and was walking along with them,
verses.24:16: but their eyes were restrained from recognizing Him.
verses.24:17: And He said to them, "What are these words that you are exchanging with one another as you walk?" And they stood still, looking downcast.
verses.24:18: And one named Cleopas answered and said to Him, "Are You the only visitor staying in Jerusalem who has not known the things that happened in it in these days?"
verses.24:19: And He said to them, "What things?" And they said to Him, "The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who was a man, a prophet, mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
verses.24:20: and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered Him to a sentence of death and crucified Him.
verses.24:21: But we were hoping that He was the One about to redeem Israel; yet indeed, besides all these things, this is the third day since these things happened.
verses.24:22: Moreover, certain women from among us astonished us; having been at the tomb early in the morning
verses.24:23: and not finding His body, they came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, who say that He is alive.
verses.24:24: And some of those with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women also had said, but Him they did not see."
verses.24:25: And He said to them, "O foolish ones and slow in heart to believe in all that the prophets spoke!
verses.24:26: Did not the Christ have to suffer these things and enter into His glory?"
verses.24:27: And beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, He interpreted for them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself.
verses.24:28: And they drew near to the village where they were going, and He acted as though He were going farther.
verses.24:29: And they strongly urged Him, saying, "Stay with us, because it is toward evening and the day has already declined." And He went in to stay with them.
verses.24:30: And it happened, while He reclined with them, that taking the bread He blessed it, and having broken it, He began giving it to them;
verses.24:31: and their eyes were opened, and they recognized Him; and He vanished from them.
verses.24:32: And they said to one another, "Was not our heart burning within us while He was speaking to us on the road, while He was opening the Scriptures to us?"
verses.24:33: And rising up that very hour, they returned to Jerusalem and found the eleven and those with them gathered together,
verses.24:34: saying, "Truly the Lord has been raised and has appeared to Simon."
verses.24:35: And they recounted the events on the road, and how He was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
verses.24:36: Now while they were speaking these things, He Himself stood in their midst and said to them, "Peace to you."
verses.24:37: But startled and becoming terrified, they thought they were seeing a spirit.
verses.24:38: And He said to them, "Why are you troubled, and why do questionings arise in your heart?
verses.24:39: See My hands and My feet, that it is I Myself; touch Me and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones just as you see Me having."
verses.24:40: And having said this, He showed them His hands and His feet.
verses.24:41: And while they were still disbelieving from joy and marveling, He said to them, "Do you have anything to eat here?"
verses.24:42: And they gave Him a piece of broiled fish;
verses.24:43: and taking it, He ate before them.
verses.24:44: Now He said to them, "These are My words that I spoke to you while I was still with you, that all things written in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms concerning Me must be fulfilled."
verses.24:45: Then He opened their mind to understand the Scriptures, and He said to them,
verses.24:46: "Thus it is written, that the Christ would suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
verses.24:47: and that repentance for forgiveness of sins would be proclaimed in His name to all the nations—beginning from Jerusalem;
verses.24:48: you are witnesses of these things.
verses.24:49: And look, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you; but you remain in the city until you are clothed with power from on high."
verses.24:50: And He led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up His hands, He blessed them.
verses.24:51: And it happened, while He was blessing them, that He parted from them and was carried up into heaven.
verses.24:52: And after worshiping Him, they returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
verses.24:53: and they were continually in the temple, blessing God.

notes.1:28: Greek κεχαριτωμένη is a perfect passive participle meaning "one who has been shown favor" or "graced," emphasizing God's initiative in bestowing grace.
notes.1:35: Following the punctuation of the Greek text, ἅγιον ("holy") serves as the predicate of κληθήσεται ("will be called") with "the Son of God" in apposition; alternatively, τὸ γεννώμενον ἅγιον may be taken together as "the holy child to be born will be called the Son of God."
notes.1:37: Greek ῥῆμα means "word" or "statement" (echoed in Mary's "your word" in v. 38), though in Septuagint idiom it can also mean "thing" or "matter"; παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ literally denotes what comes "from God."
notes.1:45: Greek ὅτι may introduce the content of Mary's belief ("that there will be a fulfillment") or give the reason for her blessedness ("for there will be a fulfillment").
notes.1:74: Following the Greek text (ἐκ χειρὸς ἐχθρῶν), no possessive "our" appears before "enemies," whereas some manuscripts add ἡμῶν ("our").
notes.1:78: Greek ἀνατολή denotes "dawn" or "sunrise" and also renders the messianic title "Branch" in the Septuagint (Zech 3:8; 6:12); the future tense ἐπισκέψεται ("will visit") is translated here rather than the aorist variant ἐπεσκέψατο ("has visited").
notes.2:2: Greek prote ("first") is normally taken as the first registration under Quirinius, though some scholars interpret it comparatively as "before Quirinius was governing Syria."
notes.2:7: Greek katalyma denotes a lodging place or guest room (compare Luke 22:11) rather than necessarily a commercial inn.
notes.2:14: The earliest manuscripts read the genitive eudokias ("people of [His] good pleasure/favor"), whereas later manuscripts read the nominative eudokia ("goodwill among people").
notes.2:37: The Greek phrase heos eton ogdoekonta tessaron can mean either that Anna was eighty-four years old or that she had been a widow for eighty-four years.
notes.2:49: Greek en tois tou patros mou (literally "in the [place/things] of My Father") is an idiom meaning either "in My Father's house" or "engaged in My Father's affairs."
notes.3:2: Greek uses the singular "high priest" for both Annas and Caiaphas; Caiaphas held the office under Rome while Annas, his father-in-law and former high priest, retained the title and influence.
notes.3:22: Some early Western manuscripts quote Psalm 2:7 here ("You are My Son; today I have begotten You") instead of "You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased."
notes.3:23: The participle "when He began" (Greek archomenos) is concise and is generally understood to refer to Jesus beginning His public ministry.
notes.3:32: "Jobel" and "Sala" follow the Greek text (as in Codex Vaticanus), corresponding to "Obed" and "Salmon" in the Hebrew Old Testament and other manuscripts.
notes.3:36: "Cainan" appears between Shelah and Arphaxad following the Septuagint of Genesis 11:12-13, though it is not found in the Masoretic Hebrew text.
notes.4:4: Some later manuscripts add "but by every word of God" (cf. Matt 4:4; Deut 8:3), which is absent from the earliest Greek witnesses.
notes.4:16: The Greek text spells the town name "Nazara," an early alternate form of Nazareth.
notes.4:18: This reading combines Isaiah 61:1-2 with Isaiah 58:6 ("to send out the oppressed in liberty"); later manuscripts add "to heal the brokenhearted" from Isaiah 61:1.
notes.4:44: The earliest manuscripts read "Judea" (likely used broadly for the whole land of the Jews), whereas some later manuscripts read "Galilee" in harmonization with Mark 1:39.
notes.5:10: Greek zōgrōn literally means "capturing alive," contrasting with the fishermen's ordinary catch of fish for death.
notes.5:17: The Greek text reads singular auton ("for Him to heal," referring to Jesus), whereas some manuscripts read plural autous ("to heal them").
notes.5:34: "The sons of the bridal chamber" is a literal Semitic idiom referring to the wedding guests or attendants of the bridegroom.
notes.5:38: Greek blēteon ("must be put") is the only verbal adjective of obligation in the New Testament; the verse also distinguishes neos ("new" in age, for the wine) from kainos ("fresh" or unused, for the wineskins).
notes.5:39: The critical Greek text reads the positive adjective chrēstos ("good"), while some later manuscripts read the comparative chrēstoteros ("better").
notes.6:1: Some later manuscripts add "second-first" (deuteroproto) to "Sabbath," an obscure term absent from the earliest manuscripts.
notes.6:12: Literally "in the prayer of God," an objective genitive meaning prayer directed to God.
notes.6:16: Greek "Judas of James" does not state the relationship explicitly; "son of James" is the standard rendering, though "brother of James" is also possible.
notes.6:35: The Greek phrase meden apelpizontes is debated; it can mean "expecting nothing in return" (contrasting with v. 34) or "despairing of nothing."
notes.6:48: The earliest manuscripts read "because it had been built well," whereas many later manuscripts harmonize with Matthew 7:25, reading "for it had been founded on the rock."
notes.7:19: The Greek text here reads "to Jesus" (πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν), whereas several early manuscripts read "to the Lord" (πρὸς τὸν κύριον).
notes.7:29: Verses 29–30 are punctuated as a parenthetical comment by the narrator, though some interpreters view them as a continuation of Jesus' speech. "Vindicated God" (ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν) means they acknowledged God to be righteous.
notes.7:35: "Is vindicated" uses a gnomic aorist (ἐδικαιώθη), echoing "vindicated" in 7:29; the preposition ἀπό ("by") marks the children of wisdom as those through whom wisdom's rightness is demonstrated.
notes.7:47: The conjunction ὅτι ("for") is debated: in light of the parable in 7:41–43, many read it evidentially ("as shown by the fact that she has loved much"), while others take it causally ("because she has loved much").
notes.8:3: The critical text reads "them" (referring to Jesus and the twelve), while some manuscripts read "Him."
notes.8:26: Manuscripts vary here and in 8:37 among "Gerasenes," "Gadarenes," and "Gergesenes"; the critical text reads "Gerasenes."
notes.8:28: Literally, "What to me and to You?", a Greek and Semitic idiom expressing resistance or asking what business one party has with another.
notes.8:43: The clause "who had spent her entire livelihood on physicians" is present in the critical text, though omitted by a few early manuscripts.
notes.8:48: Here, as in 8:36 and 8:50, the Greek verb sozo ("to save," cf. 8:12) is rendered "made well," reflecting its dual sense of physical healing and deliverance.
notes.9:2: Some early manuscripts (notably Codex Vaticanus) omit "the sick," reading simply "and to cure."
notes.9:28: Luke's "about eight days" reflects inclusive reckoning of the interval that Matthew 17:1 and Mark 9:2 express as "six days."
notes.9:31: The Greek word exodos literally means "departure" or "exodus," echoing Israel's Exodus while referring to Jesus' impending death, resurrection, and ascension.
notes.9:35: The earliest manuscripts read "the Chosen One," whereas later manuscripts harmonize with Matthew 17:5 and Mark 9:7 to read "the Beloved."
notes.9:51: The Greek term analempsis ("taking up" or "ascension") opens Luke's travel narrative to Jerusalem and looks ahead to Jesus' passion, resurrection, and ascension.
notes.9:55: Many later manuscripts add to this verse, "and said, 'You do not know what kind of spirit you are of; for the Son of Man did not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them,'" which is absent from the earliest manuscripts.
notes.10:1: The critical text reads "seventy-two" (also in 10:17), whereas many manuscripts read "seventy"; both numbers have Old Testament precedents (e.g., the nations in Genesis 10 in the Septuagint vs. Masoretic Text, or the elders in Numbers 11).
notes.10:18: The imperfect verb "I was watching" paired with the aorist participle "fall" depicts a vivid sighting of Satan's sudden downfall, viewed by interpreters either as taking place during the mission of the seventy-two or as a prophetic vision of his defeat.
notes.10:38: The critical text concludes with "welcomed Him," omitting the clarifying addition "into her house" found in many later manuscripts.
notes.10:42: The reading "few things are needed, or one" (combining a literal reference to a simple meal with the single spiritual necessity) is strongly attested in early Alexandrian witnesses, while other manuscripts shorten it to "one thing is needed" or "few things are needed."
notes.11:2: The earliest manuscripts preserve Luke's shorter form of the Lord's Prayer; later manuscripts expand verses 2-4 to harmonize with Matthew 6:9-13.
notes.11:3: Greek epiousion is a rare word of debated meaning, variously understood as "daily," "necessary for existence," or "for the coming day."
notes.11:8: Greek anaideia literally means "shamelessness" or "audacity," understood either as the petitioner's bold persistence or as the host's desire to avoid social shame.
notes.11:17: Literally "house upon house falls," an expression either depicting houses collapsing one upon another in ruin or paralleling a household divided against itself.
notes.11:41: Greek ta enonta ("the things that are inside") is debated, referring either to the contents of the cup and dish (material wealth) or to what is within the heart.
notes.12:5: Greek geenna (Gehenna), originally the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, used for the place of final punishment.
notes.12:20: Literally "they are demanding," an impersonal third-person plural idiom functioning as a passive.
notes.12:25: Greek pechus (a cubit, about 18 inches) is used figuratively for a small increment, and helikia can mean either "lifespan" or "stature."
notes.12:29: Greek meteorizomai, occurring only here in the New Testament, literally refers to being lifted in mid-air, hence unsettled or held in anxious suspense.
notes.12:46: Greek dichotomeo literally means "cut in two," though some interpreters understand it figuratively as severe punishment or expulsion.
